title: Frequency upconversion of infrared signals via molecular cavity optomechanical systems with gain
authors: Shu-Xian Quan, Fen Zou, Yong Li
abstract: Molecular cavity optomechanical systems have recently emerged as a promising platform for enhancing infrared detection sensitivity, owing to their ability to up-convert low-frequency infrared (IR) photons to visible frequency range. Generally, under red-detuned pumping in such systems, the ideal conversion efficiency of the IR signal approaches 1. To overcome this efficiency constraint, we propose a scheme that incorporates gain into the infrared cavity of a molecular cavity optomechanical system comprising two cavities and an ensemble of N molecules. The upconversion process, which relies on IR absorption and Raman scattering associated with specific vibrational modes, is significantly amplified by the incorporation of gain under the red-detuned conditions. Moreover, our analysis demonstrates that the added noise is maintained near 0.5.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates enhancing infrared-to-visible frequency upconversion using molecular cavity optomechanical systems. By introducing controlled gain into the IR cavity, the authors show that conversion efficiencies can be significantly boosted while keeping the added noise low and stable near 0.5. This suggests a viable pathway for highly sensitive quantum detection based on engineered cavity dynamics.
main_problem: The primary goal is enhancing the efficiency of frequency upconversion of low-frequency infrared (IR) signals to the visible (VIS) range using molecular cavity optomechanical systems.
main_result: The incorporation of gain into the IR cavity significantly boosts the upconversion efficiency while maintaining the associated added noise at a low and controllable level, near 0.5.
method: The analysis uses quantum Langevin equations (QLEs) solved in the frequency domain via Fourier transforms to determine input-output relations for the coupled optomechanical system.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a molecular cavity optomechanical system comprising two cavities and an ensemble of N molecules. The dynamics are modeled by coupling optical fields ($\omega_a, \omega_c$) to intrinsic molecular vibrational modes ($\omega_b$), with the key addition being gain in the IR cavity.
key_observables: Conversion efficiency ($T_{AS}^{ac}$), added noise power ($	ext{n}_{	ext{add}}(\omega)$), and output field spectra $ ar{S}_{a,out}(\omega)$.
important_parameters: Detunings ($\Delta$), decay rates ($\kappa_a, \kappa_c, \gamma_B$), coupling strengths ($G_a, G_c$), and the gain-induced effective dissipation rate ($\zeta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes negligible intrinsic losses for the two single-sided cavities when deriving QLEs, and that $\hbar\omega/k_B T \gg 1$ for noise treatment.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate system schematics (Fig. 1), stability diagrams and conversion efficiency vs. frequency (Fig. 2), and show the dependence of conversion efficiency and added noise on key parameters like decay rates ($\kappa_a, \kappa_c$) and coupling strengths ($G_a, \zeta$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the Hamiltonian and deriving QLEs for the coupled system. It then linearizes these equations, transforms them into matrix form in the frequency domain, and calculates output correlations to determine conversion efficiency and added noise under various parameter regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced quantum optics techniques (QLEs, fluctuation analysis) to a molecular/nanoscale system, demonstrating how engineered gain can overcome fundamental efficiency limits in quantum signal processing.
